facts: The English wheel only adds deformation: a sheet formed past the target cannot be formed back, so under-forming is recoverable and over-forming is not; approach the target in steps.
Orientation sets the curvature direction: rot 0 (strips along y) makes the height change mainly along x, rot 90 (strips along x) mainly along y.
A strip is a 10 mm wide wheeling track; the strips of a zigzag overlap or nearly touch (spacing 2.4-12 mm), so N follows from the working-area size.

More strips (larger N) and longer strips add more deformation per pass; the deformation concentrates in the working area, but the whole sheet bends with it, including the margins and the band next to the gripper.

Work hardening: every further pass over an already-wheeled spot adds about 0.80 times what the previous pass added there (the simulator's hardening setting), so repeated passes have diminishing returns.

With one working area the whole sheet curls into a cylinder whose axis follows the strips (rot 0: axis along the feed); a small working area concentrates the curl near itself, a large one curls the sheet uniformly.
Heights are measured relative to the sheet's own best-fit plane: the gripper holds the bottom edge, but the sheet's rigid position and tilt are not part of the shape.
